preserved_objections.basis: The proposed phononic crystal structures would actually increase shock-induced contact by creating stress concentration points at the crystal boundaries, contrary to the claimed reduction effect

Violates the boundary condition of maintaining sufficient structural integrity for shock survival as phononic crystals inherently create weak points that would fail catastrophically at 10000g shock levels

The provided evidence [doi:10.1109/iic.2015.7150884] demonstrates that comb finger structural integrity is paramount for shock survival, and introducing phononic crystals directly contradicts this fundamental requirement

The predicted 2-3 times reduction in shock-induced contact is unsupported by any evidence and likely equals the baseline performance since phononic crystals would only redistribute rather than reduce shock energy

Fabricating two-dimensional phononic crystal structures on MEMS comb fingers at the required nanoscale precision is impossible with current CMOS MEMS foundry capabilities as noted in [doi:10.3390/mi17060732]
The testable prediction fails to pin down which specific phononic crystal pattern geometry will achieve the claimed 50% reduction, making the measurement impossible to validate conclusively
